'''William David Arnett''' (born 1940) is a Regents Professor of Astrophysics at [[Steward Observatory]], [[University of Arizona]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.as.arizona.edu/people/faculty/w-david-arnett |title=W. David Arnett |publisher=As.arizona.edu |accessdate=December 9, 2013}}</ref> known for his research on [[supernova]] explosions, the formation of  [[neutron stars]] or [[black holes]] by gravitational collapse, and the [[nucleosynthesis|synthesis of elements in stars]]; he is author of the monograph ''Supernovae and Nucleosynthesis'' which deals with these topics.<ref>{{cite book|last=Arnett|first=David|title=Supernovae and Nucleosynthesis: An Investigation of the History of Matter, from the Big Bang to the Present|publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |date=1996|isbn=978-0-691-01147-9}}</ref>
Arnett pioneered the application of supercomputers to astrophysical problems, including neutrino radiation hydrodynamics,<ref>{{cite journal|author= W. D. Arnett|date= 1966|journal= Canadian Journal of Physics|volume= 44|pages= 2553–2594|doi= 10.1139/p66-210|title= Gravitational Collapse and Weak Interactions|issue= 11|bibcode = 1966CaJPh..44.2553A |hdl= 2060/19670009027|hdl-access= free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=W. D. Arnett|date=1977|journal= Astrophysical Journal|volume= 218| page=815|doi=10.1086/155738|title=Neutrino trapping during gravitational collapse of stars|bibcode = 1977ApJ...218..815A |doi-access=free}}</ref> nuclear reaction networks,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=W. D. Arnett |author2=J. W. Truran|date=1969|journal= Astrophysical Journal|volume= 157|page= 339|doi=10.1086/150072|title=Carbon-Burning Nucleosynthesis at Constant Temperature|bibcode = 1969ApJ...157..339A }}</ref> instabilities and explosions,<ref>{{cite journal|author=W. D. Arnett|date=1969|journal= Nature|volume= 222|pages= 359–361|doi=10.1038/222359b0|title=Pulsars and Neutron Star Formation|issue=5191|bibcode = 1969Natur.222..359A |s2cid=4212202}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=W. D. Arnett|date=1969|journal= Astrophysics and Space Science |volume= 5|pages= 180–212|doi=10.1007/BF00650291|title=A possible model of supernovae: Detonation of12C|issue=2|bibcode = 1969Ap&SS...5..180A |s2cid=120310982}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=B. Fryxell|author2= W. D. Arnett|author3=E. Mueller|date=1991|journal= Astrophysical Journal|volume=367|page= 619|doi=10.1086/169657|title=Instabilities and clumping in SN 1987A. I - Early evolution in two dimensions|bibcode = 1991ApJ...367..619F |doi-access=free}}</ref> supernova light curves,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=S. W. Falk|author2= W. D. Arnett|date= 1977|journal= Astrophysical Journal|volume= 33|page= 515|doi=10.1086/190440|title=Radiation Dynamics, Envelope Ejection, and Supernova Light Curves|bibcode = 1977ApJS...33..515F }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= W. I - Analytic solutions for the early part of the light curve|bibcode = 1982ApJ...253..785A }}</ref> and turbulent convective flow in two <ref>{{cite journal|author=G. Bazan|author2= W. D. Arnett|date= 1994|title=Convection, Nucleosynthesis, and Core Collapse|journal= Astrophysical Journal|volume= 433|page= 41|doi=10.1086/187543|bibcode=1994ApJ...433L..41B|doi-access= free}}</ref> and three dimensions.<ref>{{cite journal|author=C. Meakin|author2= W. D. Arnett|date= 2007|journal= Astrophysical Journal|volume= 667|issue= 1|pages=448–475|doi=10.1086/520318|title=Turbulent Convection in Stellar Interiors. I. ==Academic career==
Arnett received his BS degree from the [[University of Kentucky]] in 1961 and his MS and PhD degrees in physics from [[Yale University]] in 1963 and 1965, advised by [[A. G. W. Cameron]]. After postdoctoral work with [[W. A. Fowler]]  at the [[California Institute of Technology]] and [[Fred Hoyle]] at the Institute of Theoretical Astronomy (now [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge|Institute of Astronomy]]) of [[Cambridge University]], he served briefly on the faculties of [[Rice University]] (working with [[Donald Clayton]]), [[University of Texas]] and [[University of Illinois]] before becoming the B. and E. Sunny Distinguished Service Professor at the [[University of Chicago]] and then Regents Professor <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arizona.edu/about/awards-honors/regents-professors |title=Regents Professors &#124; The University of Arizona, Tucson, Arizona |publisher=Arizona.edu |accessdate=December 9, 2013}}</ref> at the [[University of Arizona]].

*[[Henry Norris Russell Lectureship]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://aas.org/about/grants-and-prizes/henry-norris-russell-lectureship |title=Henry Norris Russell Lectureship &#124; American Astronomical Society |publisher=Aas.org |accessdate=December 9, 2013 |archive-date=January 19, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119022215/http://aas.org/about/grants-and-prizes/henry-norris-russell-lectureship |url-status=dead }}</ref> of the [[American Astronomical Society]], 2012.
* Marcel Grossmann Award, International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics (ICRA), 2012<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icra.it/mg/awards/#13th |title=Marcel Grossmann Awards |publisher=Icra.it |accessdate=December 9, 2013}}</ref>
*[[Hans Bethe Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/bethe.cfm |title=Hans A. Bethe Prize |publisher=Aps.org |date=April 16, 2013 |accessdate=December 9, 2013}}</ref> of the [[American Physical Society]], 2009

* S. Chandrasekhar Lecturer, [[S.N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences]], Kolkata, India, 2007
* [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]], 1987 <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1987&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate=September 23, 2020}} </ref>
* Member, [[National Academy of Sciences]], 1985
* Member, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], 1985
* Alexander von [[Humboldt Prize]] (senior scientist), 1981
* [[Yale University]] Distinguished Graduate Award in Physical Sciences and Engineering (with J. W. Truran), 1980
* [[University of Kentucky]] Honorary Doctorate of Sciences, 2016
* Fellow of the [[American Astronomical Society]], 2020
